title: Practice: Effect of Surface Area on Rate

questions.stem: A student reacts 5 g of large marble chips with excess HCl, then repeats with 5 g of marble powder. Both experiments use the same concentration and volume of acid. Which statement about the results is correct?

options.text: The powder produces more gas overall because it has more surface area
The powder reacts faster but both produce the same total volume of gas
The chips react faster because they are larger
The powder reacts faster and produces more gas

questions.explanation: Both experiments use the same mass of calcium carbonate (5 g) and excess acid, so the same amount of CO2 is produced in total. The powder has a much greater surface area, so the rate is faster (steeper curve initially). The total volume of gas is determined by the amount of reactant, not the surface area.

questions.stem: Coal dust explosions in mines are extremely dangerous, yet large lumps of coal burn relatively slowly. What explains this difference?

options.text: Coal dust is a different chemical substance to coal lumps
Coal dust has an enormously larger surface area, allowing extremely rapid reaction with oxygen in the air
Coal dust is at a higher temperature than coal lumps
There is more oxygen available in mines

questions.explanation: Fine coal dust has a vastly greater total surface area compared to the same mass as lumps. This means many more carbon particles are exposed to oxygen simultaneously. The combustion reaction occurs so rapidly across the huge surface area that it becomes explosive. This same principle applies to flour dust and other combustible powders.

questions.stem: A student investigates the effect of surface area by reacting different sizes of calcium carbonate with HCl. She must control other variables. Which variables should she keep constant?

options.text: Only the volume of acid
Mass of calcium carbonate, concentration and volume of acid, and temperature
Only the temperature
The size of the calcium carbonate pieces and the temperature

questions.explanation: To make it a fair test, only one variable (surface area/particle size) should change. All other factors that affect rate must be kept constant: mass of CaCO3 (same amount of reactant), concentration and volume of HCl (same amount of acid), and temperature. This ensures any difference in rate is due to surface area alone.

questions.stem: A solid cube of metal with 1 cm sides has a surface area of 6 cm². If it is cut into 8 identical smaller cubes (each 0.5 cm sides), what is the new total surface area?

options.text: 6 cm²
12 cm²
24 cm²
48 cm²

questions.explanation: Each small cube has sides of 0.5 cm, so its surface area is 6 x (0.5)² = 6 x 0.25 = 1.5 cm². With 8 small cubes: 8 x 1.5 = 12 cm². Cutting the cube in half along each dimension doubles the total surface area from 6 to 12 cm². Smaller pieces = more total surface area for the same mass.

questions.stem: Catalytic converters in cars use platinum and rhodium coated onto a honeycomb structure. Why is a honeycomb structure used rather than a solid block of metal?

options.text: The honeycomb is cheaper to manufacture
The honeycomb structure maximises the surface area for exhaust gases to contact the catalyst
Solid blocks would melt in the exhaust system
The honeycomb filters out particulate matter

questions.explanation: The honeycomb structure provides an enormous surface area in a small volume. This maximises contact between the exhaust gases (CO, NOx, unburnt hydrocarbons) and the catalyst surface, ensuring the most efficient conversion of pollutants to less harmful products. The catalyst is coated as a thin layer to maximise exposure while using minimal precious metal.
